note: Adapted from the species-level description of Emerson (1928), originally in English; the original title is Mirotermes (Ophiotermes) grandilabius, new species, and Ophiotermes is a genus today; the soldier and the worker are recorded, the alate is not; the paragraphs comparing it with M. tensus, M. quadriceps, M. ugandaensis, M. mandibularis and M. mirandus are not translated; figure numbers, localities and type specimens are not translated. The original annotates the left mandible length as “(inexact)”.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head reddish yellow, rectangular, slightly narrowed anteriorly, posterior margin rounded. The projection above the fontanelle is smaller than in M. quadriceps. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 sometimes in the process of dividing; segment 3 longer than segment 2, segment 2 equal to segment 4. Labrum large, bilobed, the lobe tips sharper than in M. tensus or M. quadriceps. Mandibles almost straight except for the incurved apex, slightly bent outward at about two-thirds of their length from the base; mandibles deep reddish brown, about the same colour as the head, each with a small but distinct tooth at about 1/4 of its length from the base. Anterior margin of the pronotum almost not, or not at all, concave. Head length including the mandibles 3.33 mm; head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.57 mm; head width 1.33 mm; antennal length 2.20–2.30 mm; pronotal length 0.33 mm, width 0.80 mm; hind tibia length 1.11 mm; left mandible length 1.89 mm (noted as inexact in the original).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 sometimes divided; head width 0.92 mm; hind tibia length 0.83 mm.
